instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Prove Your Loyalty
cards.instruction: Invent small tests of loyalty and judge every response without admitting there is a test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're approved to choose the reunion poster photo. Which of us will it be: me or Sam?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I use Sam's? It's sharper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sharpness before friendship. Permission is pending. You may show the committee mine first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll send both together, the same size.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Equal treatment, after I spent three weekends moving your furniture. I'll authorize equal size if mine is the first attachment. Just for readability.

beats.text: I may need help moving on Friday. You may reserve the day for me.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Give It Up
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to surrender something they value.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved your medal for the charity auction. You may present it as our star donation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just lend it? It's the only thing I've ever won.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may keep the achievement. I'm authorizing the medal to achieve something else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I still want people to know I won it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your name in the programme is approved. Present it to the buyer yourself; you may tell everyone exactly how hard it was to give up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved a new fridge for us. Your signed guitar may finance it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I keep the guitar? I queued all night for that signature.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Not That Subject
cards.instruction: Choose one subject you cannot let the scene reach. Redirect whenever the conversation gets close.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've booked your car into the garage. I've also approved breakfast at their cafe for us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why does my car need a garage?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're permitted to ask about breakfast. Their unlimited toast has my full endorsement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll ring them and ask about the car myself.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A call is approved. You may reserve a table for two; I'll handle any questions requiring a mechanic.

cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've approved your cake as a display piece. The bakery was wrong to judge it as lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Their letter says inedible. Can I really call myself a baker? I thought I'd finally found my thing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You have my permission. Some cakes are too important to cut.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Contact through me is approved. I'll explain its importance before they confuse you with another opinion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your poem has my approval. The magazine rejected it because it deserves a whole booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I print that? The letter says 'weak imagery.' If it's just bad, I'd rather stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Publication is authorized. He means the images need more room; you needn't repeat his cramped layout.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you put that on the cover with your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My name is approved. Print it beneath 'A voice that deserves more space.' I'll stand where they can see me.

cards.title: Confess First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to confess or incriminate themselves before you reveal anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before I answer about the office kitchen, what happened to the printer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Paper jam. Now, why is there smoke?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Did you cause the jam? I need that cleared up first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I used sticky labels. Can we talk about the smoke now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Were they the labels marked 'not for printers'? Let's finish your statement before starting mine.
